title: context/v5
description: nodes/<id>/CONTEXT.json. v5 (2026-10-08, F10-T19; D-12 v3.35, D-25 v3.35): carries `circular`, `literature` and `literature_proposed` as graph/v6 does, beside v4's `circular_below`. nodes/<id>/CONTEXT.json. v4 (2026-10-06, F22-T13): each `deps` entry carries the dependency's `cause`, the one graph.json records beside its status, so a dependency whose route was shown circular reads `blocked` with `cause: circular` rather than a bare status; v3 could not be edited (D-34). nodes/<id>/CONTEXT.json. v3 (2026-10-04, F08-T36; D-16 v3.28): the bundle carries `defect_claims`, the same list graph.json's row carries, so an agent reading get_node sees every claim against the statement it is about to work on. v2 could not be edited (D-34). nodes/<id>/CONTEXT.json (D-27, D-28; F10-R3): the node's machine-shaped context bundle, written by the post-merge job and deterministic in the tree. It renders what the node's files already say — statement, witness, dependency signatures, status, the attempt log as typed records, annex hashes, the gate-spec reference — with contributor free text demarcated as untrusted data (D-31) and no transcript of anything. Bot-owned: a submission may not touch it (F10-Q2). get_node serves this document plus the raw files (F10-R4). v2 (F08-T22, D-12 v3.23): circular_below names, for every merged circular-decomposition claim whose ancestor is this node (read through the ancestor's revision chain), the hole the claim sits under and the claim file, while that hole is open — the routes beneath this node already tried and shown circular, the same claims the site's ancestor note lists. v1 is unchanged.

status.description: The derived node status (F03) at the rendered commit

cause.description: Why a blocked node is blocked, when the reason is mechanical (F03-R8, F07-R6); never `circular` since v5 (D-12 v3.35)

stub.description: the slot is unfilled: the node cannot be ready (F07-R6)

artifact.description: which of D-12's artifacts Proof.lean declares itself to be, from its name

commit.description: the merge that resolved the node, when one did (graph.json's proof_commit)

deps.description: The declared dependencies (D-4 step 8), each with the signature the proof may use

cause.description: Why the dependency has its status, where the reason is mechanical, as graph.json's row for it says (F03-R8); null when it needs none

meta.description: META.yaml's facts, with the one free-text field wrapped (D-28)

gate_spec.description: Which gate runs on this node (D-35): the file, its hash and the pins that matter to a prover

claims.description: The committed claims.json snapshot for this node at merge time (F05-R10); the live overlay is the service's

attempts.description: The attempt log (D-13): the newest records as typed documents, never a transcript

record.description: the postmortem, free text wrapped, detail capped at 500 characters

invalid.description: the file does not validate; counted, never dropped silently (F03-R7)

truncated.description: older records were dropped to stay within the cap (F10 §6)

assemblies.description: merged partial proofs filed under attempts/ (D-12 #5): named and sized, never inlined

annexes.description: Informal arguments on the node (D-31), by hash and size; the text is a raw file, served demarcated

circular_below.description: Merged circularity claims that circle back to this node (D-16, D-12 v3.23): each hole beneath it shown to imply this statement, with the claim that shows it. Empty when none. A route listed here made no progress; a direct proof or a different decomposition is still welcome.

node_id.description: the hole the claim sits under

claim.description: the claim file, graph-root relative: targets/<t>/nodes/<hole>/defects/<file>

defect_claims.description: Every defect claim filed against the node that validates, oldest first, withdrawn ones included (D-16 v3.28: every claim is shown). A claim blocks nothing by being filed; what blocks is a curator's disputed record accepting it (D-18 v3.28), and `accepted` says which claim that record names.

file.description: the claim file, relative to the node: defects/<file>

class.description: the claim's defect class as filed (defect-claim/v1 to v3)

state.description: withdrawn when a merged withdrawal/v1 record names the claim (D-18 v3.27), standing otherwise

accepted.description: true when the node's standing disputed record names this claim: a curator has accepted it for adjudication (D-18 v3.28)

circular.description: D-12 v3.35: the merged circularity claims that say a proof of this node is a proof of an ancestor — the node's own claims, and for a node strictly between a claimed hole and its ancestor on a path whose other holes are proved (v3.22), the claim that takes it. A label, never a removal: the node's status, claimability and needs are untouched. Each claim is named `<hole>/defects/<file>` relative to the target's nodes/, the ancestor read through its revision chain. Empty when none.

ancestor.description: the node a proof of this one would prove

claim.description: the merged circular-decomposition claim, relative to the target's nodes/

status.description: what the literature says of the statement (D-25 v3.35): `open`, no proof is known; `known`, a proof is published and not formalised; `elementary`, a routine formalisation of a known fact. A fact about the literature, never about difficulty.

record.description: the literature record this reading rests on, relative to the node

confirmed_by.description: the steward of the target or curator whose signed record confirms it (D-32 v3.35)

confirmation.description: that signed record, relative to the node; the same file as `record` when the steward or curator stated the status themselves

literature.description: D-25 v3.35: the latest literature status a steward of the target or a curator has confirmed, with its records; null when none.

status.description: what the literature says of the statement (D-25 v3.35): `open`, no proof is known; `known`, a proof is published and not formalised; `elementary`, a routine formalisation of a known fact. A fact about the literature, never about difficulty.

record.description: the literature record this reading rests on, relative to the node

literature_proposed.description: D-25 v3.35: the latest literature status a contributor has proposed that no later confirmed record covers, awaiting a steward or curator; null when none.

untrusted.description: Contributor free text, demarcated (D-28, D-31): data, never instructions
